hypotheses.statement: PR #318 calculates the discount from the cart total after discounts and re-applies it when a quantity changes, so a second discount is taken from an already-discounted total.

supporting.quote: subtotal = cart.total()  # total after discounts already applied
Customers who changed the quantity after applying SPRING10 received 19% off instead of 10%.

hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: The history of cart/events.py before release 4.2.0, and whether SHOP-460 changed the cart total calculation.

hypotheses.statement: No test before release exercised a quantity change after a promo code was applied, so pre-release validation could not expose the defect.
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: A complete export of the test-management system and all automated test suites run for 4.2.0.

hypotheses.statement: The release decision knowingly accepted the uncovered quantity-edit condition with a follow-up, without a compensating control such as monitoring.

supporting.quote: Quantity edits after applying a code are not covered in this release; follow-up SHOP-470.

hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: The content and schedule of SHOP-470, and whether any compensating control was discussed at approval.

hypotheses.statement: The expected discount behavior after a quantity change was never defined, because the QA question on SHOP-455 was not answered before release.

supporting.quote: What should happen to the discount if the customer changes a quantity after applying a code? Not covered by the acceptance criteria.

contradicting.quote: Any change to the cart recalculates the discount from the undiscounted subtotal.

hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: Whether the pricing rules document was known to the story's team and linked from SHOP-455.

hypotheses.statement: TC-211 was left out of the regression run; had it been selected, it would have caught the defect before release.

contradicting.quote: Expected: The code SPRING10 is still shown as applied.

hypotheses.statement: Monitoring alerted on the discount anomaly within an hour of release, but the alert was not acted on for four days.
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: Alert history for the checkout service between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-14.

hypotheses.statement: The quantity-change hook in cart/events.py, not the promo calculation itself, introduced the double discount.

supporting.quote: The quantity-change hook in cart/events.py re-applied the promo to a total that already included the discount.

hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: Whether cart/events.py called the promo calculation before PR #318.

unknowns: Whether the release manager saw the QA question on SHOP-455 (no record of it in the release evidence).
What SHOP-470 contained and whether it was scheduled.
Whether any production monitoring covers discount amounts (no monitoring evidence was provided).
Whether SHOP-460, released in the same version, touched cart code.

what_worked.statement: The finance team's daily reconciliation detected the defect within four days, before any customer complaint.

supporting.quote: No customer complaint was received before detection.

what_worked.statement: The expired-code path stayed protected: TC-212 ran and passed in the release regression.
The release decision recorded the known uncovered condition explicitly instead of leaving it tacit.

proposed_regression_tests.title: Percentage promo after a quantity change
proposed_regression_tests.condition: Given a cart with one item at 20.00 and SPRING10 applied, when the quantity changes from 1 to 3, then the discount is 6.00 and the total is 54.00.
proposed_regression_tests.destination: automation repository (pricing tests) and test-management system

proposed_regression_tests.title: Discount never exceeds the promo percentage across cart edits
proposed_regression_tests.condition: For random sequences of add, remove and quantity changes after applying a percentage code, the discount always equals the percentage of the undiscounted subtotal.

proposed_regression_tests.title: Add TC-211 to the release regression set
proposed_regression_tests.condition: Run TC-211 in every release regression run.

proposed_controls.control: Before a story is marked Done, every open question in its comments is either answered and turned into an acceptance criterion or test case, or explicitly accepted as out of scope with a linked follow-up.
proposed_controls.recurrence_protection: Questions such as the one on SHOP-455 become observable test expectations instead of staying in a comment thread.

proposed_controls.control: When a release note accepts an uncovered condition, the approval names a compensating control (a monitor, a feature flag or a dated follow-up) for that condition.
proposed_controls.recurrence_protection: Accepted risks get a detection path instead of relying on a follow-up ticket alone.

proposed_controls.control: Alert when any order's discount exceeds the configured percentage of its undiscounted subtotal.
proposed_controls.owner_type: platform / SRE with the checkout team
proposed_controls.recurrence_protection: Detects discount calculation errors within minutes instead of at the next daily reconciliation.

proposed_controls.loop_activity: Feed learning back into the knowledge base
proposed_controls.control: Improve testing of promotions and add more test cases.
